correctness.rationale: For every integer B>=2, n>=1 and every starting index, the stated 2-binomial fingerprint is precisely (n,r,T), where r is the number of markers and T their total relative offset, since scattered 01=T-r(r-1)/2 and the other two-letter counts follow at fixed length and weight. For r=0 or 1 the factor is immediate. For r>=2 the markers are consecutive powers B^a,...,B^(a+r-1); their sum gives T=A_r B^a-rs with A_r=(B^r-1)/(B-1). Exclusion of the immediately preceding marker confines a>=1 to half-open T intervals [(A_r-r)B^a,(A_r-r/B)B^a). Adjacent levels cannot overlap because B^r-1>=r(B-1/B) for B,r>=2, with equality only at B=r=2 and the upper endpoint open. The a=0 starts are only s=0,1 and give T=A_r,A_r-r; these lie below the positive levels except B=r=2, when they equal 3,1, the only level-one T equals 2, and higher levels start at 4. Thus T and r uniquely determine a,s and every factor. Explicit integer start windows L_{a,r}=max(B^(a-1)+1,B^(a+r-1)-n+1) for a>=1 and max(0,B^(r-1)-n+1) for a=0, with U_{a,r}=min(B^a,B^(a+r)-n), exhaust the factors with >=2 ones and neither double-count nor omit intervals; the n+1 zero/singleton words all occur at sufficiently isolated large powers. The resulting finite double sum counts all factors. At n=2, distinct 01 and 10 have the same first-order fingerprint, proving sharp order two. The geometric support is B-automatic (regular 10* base-B representations) and not eventually periodic (unbounded gaps and infinitely many ones). Checked the exact B=2,r=2 and end-exclusive boundary cases. A fresh separate exact-integer factor/sum/formula implementation compared 2,400,960 windows across bases 2..9 and n=1..120 with 960 formula comparisons; zero mismatches. These finite diagnostics are supplementary, not proof of the universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality for the all-base 2-binomial factor-reconstruction theorem, qualified by the preexisting general identity scattered-01 = positional moment minus binomial(weight,2), classical factor-complexity methods, and an extensive same-object reflection-complexity classification. The published same-object theorem enumerates and pairs powers-of-B factors under reversal but does not assert or imply injectivity of the scattered-subsequence fingerprint. Known binomial-faithfulness theorems apply to Sturmian, Tribonacci, and selected balanced/billiard language classes with hypotheses the geometric-power-support word does not satisfy. The closest Rigo–Stipulanti–Whiteland sparse nonrecurrent example requires order 3, not 2. Other published automatic words have distinct languages. The first-level arithmetic separation and exact all-base window formula remain unlocated as prior claims. This is an incremental, not foundational, new classification; unindexed equivalent formulations and stronger theorems are residual priority risks.
residual_risks: The closely related published same-object reversal-complexity theorem already proves a full factor language count and uniqueness from first two gap positions; the submitted exact factor enumeration may be a short re-expression. Originality is specifically the all-base (r,T) collision exclusion, not the factor language itself.
Unindexed or differently named Parikh-matrix/binomial-class result, or a general sparse-word criterion specialized to powers, may predate this proof. Failed searches are not novelty proof.
The 2025 Richomme primary paper was only read in abstract and related citations; no whole-document exclusion is claimed.
Some selected thesis chapters and primary PDF portions, not every page of every very long source, were read; no blanket whole-document exclusion follows.

value.rationale: Order-two scattered-subsequence reconstruction of an entire natural aperiodic automatic language is a motivated exact combinatorics-on-words invariant. The proof gives the optimal reconstruction order for every B and factor length and an exact arithmetic factor-complexity census, not an arbitrary finite slice. In contrast, the Rigo et al. sparse nonrecurrent morphic word has order-two collisions and needs order three; the Tribonacci/Sturmian examples are recurrent and structurally different. The uniform nonrecurrent sparse power-marker family therefore provides a natural sharp positive case. Its exact formula is useful for complexity and algorithmic factor fingerprinting, though the counting apparatus overlaps a published same-object reflection census; no broad classification of all sparse words or downstream theorem is asserted.

final_claim: For every integer B>=2, the indicator word supported at indices {1,B,B^2,...} has distinct length-n factors separated by their order-2 scattered subsequence fingerprints for all n>=1; binomial order 2 is sharp. Its factor/two-binomial complexity is n+1 plus the explicit finite sum of counts of all integer start intervals containing consecutive B^a,...,B^(a+r-1) markers and excluding neighboring markers.
limitations: No result for nongeometric sparse supports, arbitrary binary sequences or alphabets larger than two. Complexity is a finite interval sum, not an optimized elementary closed form.
The independent finite arithmetic scan is a bounded diagnostic, not an infinite proof; correctness follows from the reviewed half-open inequality and exact start-window argument.
Same-word published reflection complexity overlaps factor enumeration; this finding does not claim that known identity, factor membership or automaticity as new.

Originality is best-of-knowledge; obscure equivalent prior art or a stronger sparse-word criterion remains possible. Some relevant sources were inspected in selected sections only; one background paper abstract only.
Publication not_ready is a confidentiality/transport limitation, not C/O/V scientific failure. No external human expert attestation, Lean proof or GitHub publication is claimed.
